solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Agent commandeers shelter for dwarf

indicators.note: to commandeer is to seize and occupy, so the agent's word takes the shelter word inside it

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
lee is shelter from the wind

explanation.surface: A secret agent seizes a refuge to house a small person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dwarf' is the name of one of Snow White's seven dwarfs, not a description.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepy is one of the seven dwarfs in the Snow White story, so the clue's dwarf names him.

clue.text: Stay beside the sea

definitions.meaning: a stay is a prop or support, as in a beam used to hold up a wall
the land at the water's edge, the coast

explanation.surface: An invitation to remain at the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop holding up a structure is a stay, and the strip of land along the sea is the coast; one word covers both.

clue.text: Monarch's followed round to be protected

indicators.note: the word for followed goes round the monarch's letter, enclosing it

parts.note: ensued means came after, followed
R stands for Rex or Regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A king's entourage surrounds him for his safety.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', a link joining wordplay to the definition, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Made safe or secured against harm is a sense of the verb meaning guarantee or make certain.

clue.text: 101 going into show that's telling the future

indicators.note: the number's letters enter the word for show, sitting inside it

parts.note: to present is to show or display
in Roman numerals C is 100 and I is 1

explanation.surface: A beginners' course seems to be part of a fortune-telling show.
explanation.walkthrough: 101 suggests an introductory course, but here it is just Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescient person has foreknowledge, effectively foretelling what will happen.

clue.text: Visual display of yellow in the atmosphere

indicators.note: the colour's letters sit in the middle of the word for atmosphere

parts.note: an aura is a distinctive atmosphere around a place or person
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: A yellow light show is seen in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold or yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern or southern lights are a natural light show in the night sky, a visual spectacle.

clue.text: Wise man supports university convention

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece below holds up the one above, so the university letter comes first

parts.note: a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A learned scholar backs an academic conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supports' places SAGE beneath U in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Customary practice, the accepted way of doing things, is a convention.

clue.text: Pick one parent — the most favourable

parts.note: to opt is to pick or choose
I is the Roman numeral for one
mum is a British word for mother

explanation.surface: Choosing just one parent is the best course.
explanation.definitionFit: The best possible or most advantageous condition is a synonym for the most favourable.

clue.text: Battle for a drink on the bar

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next, so the drink comes above the bar

parts.note: gin is an alcoholic drink
the bar is a court of law, the place where a prisoner stands

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a drink served on a pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but here it is the bar of a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry V defeated the French at this 1415 battle in northern France.

clue.text: Quality controller eats duck found in the kitchen

indicators.note: eating takes something in, so the controller's word swallows the duck letter

parts.note: a taster checks the quality of food or drink
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, hence the letter O

explanation.surface: A food inspector consumes duck in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck is the cricket zero, O, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A bread-browning appliance is a typical kitchen item, so the definition describes it by its location.

clue.text: Footballers' birds to stalk another bird

parts.note: WAGs are footballers' wives and girlfriends, birds being slang for women
to tail is to follow or stalk

explanation.surface: Footballers' girlfriends set out to follow a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: WAGs, a British tabloid term for the wives and girlfriends of footballers; 'birds' is slang for women, then 'another bird' is the real thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A small long-tailed songbird that bobs its tail is a feathered creature, so an example of a bird.

clue.text: Exploit Lily over Frenchman's occult belief

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit over the later one

parts.note: to vamp is to exploit, especially a man, by seductive wiles
an iris is a flower related to the lily family
M is the abbreviation for monsieur, a French man

explanation.surface: Taking advantage of a woman named Lily over a Frenchman's mystical faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Lily looks like a name but is the flower IRIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Belief in blood-drinking undead beings is a supernatural, occult creed.

clue.text: One included in censure is to lose value

indicators.note: the numeral is put inside the word for censure

parts.note: to deprecate is to express disapproval of, to censure
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A person criticised by others is set to fall in standing.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall in worth over time, as assets do, is the economic sense of depreciation.

clue.text: Club for men originally getting a hole in one

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word men

parts.note: in golf an ace is a hole in one

explanation.surface: A golf club for men, where someone hits a hole in one.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf setting makes 'Club' look like a golf club or society; it is a heavy weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy spiked club used as a weapon, so both words name a cudgel.

clue.text: Powerful Venetian imprisons copper for scheme

indicators.note: the Venetian's title locks the copper's letter inside it

parts.note: the doge was the ruler of Venice
a copper is a penny coin, and d was the abbreviation for a penny in old British money

explanation.surface: A Venetian ruler jails a policeman as part of a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer, but here it is a penny, d in pre-1971 British currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a trick or ruse, so a crafty plan or scheme.

clue.text: Flirting gets Penny a relationship

parts.note: d was the abbreviation for a penny in old British money
an alliance is a relationship or association

explanation.surface: A woman named Penny finds that flirting leads to a relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny looks like a woman's name; it is the old penny, d.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalliance is casual romantic play, toying with someone's affections, which is what flirting means.

clue.text: Learn to collect note for restorer

indicators.note: collecting gathers something in, so the phrase for learn takes the note inside

parts.note: to pick up a skill is to learn it
me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone is studying how to gather a musical note to revive themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic or drink that revives someone's spirits is a restorative, something that restores.

clue.text: Run after officer for help

indicators.note: the word for run comes after the officer's letters

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
to operate a business is to run it

explanation.surface: Someone sprints after an officer to get assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: Run suggests sprinting but means manage, OPERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To work together with others is to assist in a joint effort, so collaborate or help.

clue.text: Lift to reveal assembly

indicators.note: assembly means putting parts together, so the letters of these words are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A device is raised to show what a gathering looks like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assembly' rearranges TO REVEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift is the British word and elevator the American word for the same passenger hoist in a building.

clue.text: Revolutionary meets much- liked rogue

parts.note: Pancho Villa was a Mexican revolutionary leader
in means fashionable or popular, much liked

explanation.surface: A rebel encounters a beloved scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is a wicked person, a scoundrel or rogue.

clue.text: Where film star performs in the beginning

definitions.meaning: an actor works ..., on the film set
the start or outbreak of something

explanation.surface: A film actor performs from the opening.
explanation.definitionFit: The beginning of something, as of an illness or winter, is its start; read as two words it is where a film actor works.

clue.text: Met to restrict legal right of striking

indicators.note: the word for met hems in the legal right, holding it inside

parts.note: a committee sat when it met in session
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: The Metropolitan Police curtail the legal right to go on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: Met suggests London's Metropolitan Police; it means assembled, SAT. 'Striking' suggests industrial action but means prominent.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means most noticeable or prominent, so conspicuous and striking.

clue.text: Pass on purpose

definitions.meaning: to bequeath, hand on to heirs at death

explanation.surface: Something done intentionally, or something passed over.
explanation.definitionFit: To bequeath property is to leave it by testament, and resolve or determination is a person's intent.

clue.text: Foreign Office has money for charge

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for the British Foreign Office
sterling is British money

explanation.surface: The Foreign Office has funds to pay a fee.
explanation.walkthrough: Charge looks like a fee but means someone in one's care.
explanation.definitionFit: A child raised by foster parents is in their care, a ward or charge.

clue.text: Fine fields for jumpers

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
leas are meadows or fields

explanation.surface: Pleasant fields suit those who jump.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumpers could be sweaters (British) or show horses; here they are the leaping insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleas are tiny parasitic insects famous for leaping, so they are jumpers.

clue.text: Cosset girl in US city

indicators.note: the girl's name is placed in the abbreviation for the US city

parts.note: NY is New York
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Pamper a girl living in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: To nanny someone is to be overprotective, fussing over them as a nursemaid would; to pamper or cosset.

clue.text: Anon produced mundane novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of the word are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An anonymous author produced a dull novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' suggests a book but signals the letters of MUNDANE rearranged. Anon also reads as 'soon'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is short for anonymous, so it signals a work whose author is not given a name.

clue.text: Call for worker in show

parts.note: to page someone is to call them over a loudspeaker or pager
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: Summoning an employee to appear in a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a public entertainment or parade, a spectacle or show.

clue.text: Resent potentially important chap?

indicators.note: potentially means the letters could become something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone may come to resent a self-important man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potentially' rearranges RESENT. The definition alludes to Wilde's play The Importance of Being Earnest, whose hero needs to be called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Oscar Wilde's comedy the importance lies in being named this, so a man with this name is the 'important' fellow.

clue.text: Watch shows minute and seconds to start with

indicators.note: the seconds letter is placed at the start, before the record word

parts.note: a minute is a written record or note, an entry in the minutes of a meeting

explanation.surface: A watch displays both minutes and seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: Minute and seconds suggest a clock face; minute is a written record. Watch is the guard, not the timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier keeping guard stands watch, so a guard on duty is called a watch.
